# HackProof

> HackProof runs a hackathon submission for real and checks what its README claims. Nosana hosted inference (qwen/qwen3.8-27b) reads the README and plans the checks; a fresh Daytona sandbox runs the project; each claim gets a verdict (verified, refuted, inconclusive, not_checkable) from exit codes and measurements, with a receipt. Built at Daytona HackSprint Tokyo, 2026-11-15, by Masa.

Key facts (all from saved receipts in this repo):
- Real run on GitHub main through the live demo: receipt receipts/20261115065249-39e5cb.json, planner nosana-llm, 3 verified, 1 refuted, 0 inconclusive, 2 not_checkable, 26.2 s.
- Daytona sandbox creation is about 0.6 s per submission; every receipt records the sandbox id.
- The LLM only proposes; allow-listed commands and execution results decide every verdict.
- Sponsors: Daytona (core: one disposable sandbox per submission), Nosana (hosted inference planner).
